correctness.rationale: C: The source proof starts from exact zonotope support sum W(U)=sum_{ij}|U_i-U_j|, couples intrinsic U to centered independent Gaussians X,Y via chi radius, and decomposes the two-sample Gini kernel into independent h(X)/p and h(Y)/q projections plus an L2-small degenerate remainder. The key covariance Cov(h(X),X²−1)=mu/2 yields the -2/pi normalization term, avoiding a false unnormalized Gaussian variance. For fixed p the conditional LLN gives (1/p)sum f(G_i); f(x)=b+bx²/2+O(x⁴) gives the exact chi-square small-ball boundary constant (pt/b)^{p/2}/Gamma(p/2+1). The subsequence argument handles arbitrarily oscillating growing aspects. Independent mpmath/SymPy evaluation reproduced mu=1.128379167096, b=0.797884560803, v=0.162751579442 and the positive 0.014386545399 balanced variance. No rate is claimed for all p,q. value.rationale: V: The width distribution of a canonical family of centrally symmetric polytopes is geometrically natural; the finite-side p/2 angular-edge signature distinguishes discrete combinatorial size through rotation-invariant data. At balance the radial correction changes the limiting variance by a quantitatively large amount, and the unlimited aspect-ratio dichotomy goes beyond the known first two moments.

final_claim: For the ordinary intrinsic Euclidean width of K_{p,q} graphical zonotopes, the fixed-small-part non-Gaussian f(G) law has lower-edge exponent p/2; when min(p,q) grows, a centered, radial-corrected Gaussian CLT holds at any aspect ratio, with positive balanced variance 4v-2/pi.
limitations: Only standard unweighted root-vector zonotope; fixed p or growing min(p,q), not arbitrary weighted graphs.
Historical priority is qualified, independent numerical tests cannot prove limiting theorems.
